text:
The Wall Street Journal uncovered new connections in an alleged network smuggling restricted Nvidia *($NVDA)* chips into China, identifying Li Ming as a key operator behind Megaspeed alongside Alice Huang, the former executive romantically linked to Jensen Huang. The investigation found that former Megaspeed associates reportedly now run Novagate Cloud, which received at least $300M in Nvidia-related hardware after Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal no-sell list.

• *Key Operator:* Li allegedly helped direct Megaspeed and related chip-trading businesses behind the scenes. Singapore charged him with fraud in February 2025 for allegedly telling a U.S. supplier that Nvidia-equipped servers were for his local company when they were instead shipped through Malaysia to an undisclosed destination. He remains out on bail.
• *Alice Huang Connections:* Li worked with Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, for years. The couple established Century Longteng in 2021, with Li identified as its chief strategy officer in 2023. The venture was a key shareholder in Shanghai-based Century Litong until 2024.
• *Megaspeed Operations:* Megaspeed gained priority Nvidia chip access in November 2023 after identifying Alibaba *($BABA)* as an anchor customer. It provided legitimate offshore computing services to Alibaba, but the WSJ previously reported that some servers were diverted through Malaysia to Century Litong in violation of U.S. export controls. Megaspeed maintains its business is lawful.
• *New Cloud Operation:* Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal no-sell list in June 2025. Former associates reportedly now operate Novagate Cloud, established in 2025, whose Malaysian entity received at least $300M in Nvidia-equipped hardware during the first five months of 2026. Novagate claims to be an Nvidia cloud partner operating at least two Blackwell-equipped data centers. Corporate records also connect its personnel to Century Litong-associated businesses.

*Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Americans shouldn’t worry about their banks after last week’s tech outages, calling banks among the most resilient U.S. companies.*

• Bessent attributed JPMorgan’s disruption to security patching. He compared the glitch to a vaccine’s sore arm: short-term discomfort in exchange for stronger defenses.
• He said banks face cyberattacks routinely and have spent decades strengthening their defenses.

*Scott Bessent said Trump’s threat to penalize overseas data center construction targets American companies. He said U.S. support for projects in Gulf allies such as the UAE still stands.*

• *Policy Details:* Bessent said he hadn’t discussed the proposal with Trump. He thinks Trump wants to prevent key technology from moving offshore.
• *Chip Precedent:* Bessent said Taiwan makes 97% of high-end chips, creating a strategic vulnerability. He pointed to TSMC’s Arizona factories and said the administration hopes to bring substantial chip production back by the end of its term.
• *U.S. Buildout:* Asked whether the penalties could give Chinese rivals an edge, Bessent said companies can access AI computing power across borders. He urged the industry to rebuild trust with local communities to support more U.S. construction.

*Scott Bessent downplayed the risk that Nvidia’s financing of projects that buy its chips could spread trouble across the tech sector.*

• *Nvidia:* Bessent said the board slowed things down after the leadership change and that the CFO, now in charge, understands the financing. He cited strong profitability and “near unlimited” global chip demand.
• *Sell-Off:* Bessent said the decline began as Democrats gained in the polls and accelerated after Election Day. He pointed to investor fears that Democrats could slow the AI buildout, hawkish Fed remarks and tighter financial conditions. He said some investors worry the Fed could tighten too much.

*Asked whether Jensen Huang should return as Nvidia CEO, Scott Bessent said the company first needs to establish who was responsible for possible export violations.*

• *CEO Return:* CBS’s Margaret Brennan said Trump backed Huang’s return. Bessent, who had urged the board to look outside Nvidia, noted that Huang is “on the outside now.”
• *Internal Review:* Bessent said Nvidia’s committees are moving quickly to determine who knew what and whether that knowledge reached senior leadership.
• *Alice Huang:* Bessent framed corporate compliance as separate from the relationship. He said he assumed Jensen Huang was unaware of Alice Huang’s alleged ties to Chinese intelligence.

*Scott Bessent defended the U.S. approach to AI chip exports after House records showed Commerce approved sales of more than 800,000 Nvidia and AMD chips to China.*

• *Buyer Scrutiny:* CBS’s Margaret Brennan highlighted two companies linked to China’s military. Bessent cited Alibaba and said the buyers in question were businesses that deal with the military.
• *H200 Threshold:* Bessent said Trump drew a hard line at Nvidia’s H200 chip and questioned whether the U.S. needed to treat buyers differently once that threshold was set.

*The FAA says Delta Air Lines ($DAL) flights departing Atlanta and those heading there from the contiguous U.S. are facing approximately hourlong delays after an automated aircraft weight-and-balance system went offline. Delta is the only commercial airline affected by the delay program.*

• *System Failure:* The system calculates aircraft weight, including fuel, passengers and baggage, and determines the plane’s center of gravity to ensure safe weight distribution.
• *Delta Response:* The airline is using manual workarounds to safely dispatch flights while restoring automation. Delta is also coordinating with air traffic controllers to reduce congestion at its Atlanta hub.
• *Recent Disruptions:* The delays follow a nationwide ground stop last weekend that canceled thousands of flights and a separate United Airlines problem on Monday that also caused delays.

*The New York Times reports that China’s Ministry of State Security has spent at least two years secretly helping Chinese companies acquire and smuggle restricted AI chips while gathering semiconductor intelligence, part of a coordinated government effort to overcome U.S. technology restrictions.*

• *Spy Agency Operation:* Intelligence chief Chen Yixin created a team reporting directly to him to support China's “counter-blockade” campaign. A separate high-level commission, established by Xi Jinping and led by Ding Xuexiang, coordinates the broader push for technological self-reliance.
• *Intelligence Methods:* Officials say the campaign targets advanced chips and semiconductor supply chains. China's spy agency has also used businesses, researchers and other organizations to gather foreign technology intelligence.
• *Alice Huang Investigation:* U.S. officials allege Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia *($NVDA)* founder Jensen Huang, passed information about him to Beijing. Her company, Megaspeed, is also under U.S. investigation for suspected chip smuggling. Her precise role in the spy agency's campaign remains unclear, and China denies the espionage allegations.
• *Alibaba Connection:* The Times previously reported that Megaspeed may have aided a Chinese military-linked laboratory through Alibaba *($BABA)*, its customer and financial backer. Alibaba denies providing military services and says its contracts prohibit such activity.
• *U.S. Response:* The Trump administration announced new restrictions requiring overseas data centers to obtain licenses before supplying significant computing power to firms headquartered in China, Russia or Iran. The rule is expected to take effect in approximately 90 days.
TRUMP: INCLINED TO STRIKE IRAN AFTER NEW YEAR IF NO DEAL

*Trump told Fox News he is inclined to resume military strikes against Iran after the new year if no agreement is reached, according to correspondent Trey Yingst. Indirect negotiations remain ongoing.*

• *Iran Talks:* Trump described Iranian officials as “professional tap dancers,” adding, “They talk all the time, all they do is talk, but it's all BS.”

*Trump threatened to fire on Iranian vessels challenging the U.S. naval blockade, amid continued attacks on oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz.*

• *Strait of Hormuz:* Fox News Trey Yingst reported ongoing Iranian tanker attacks, including additional incidents within the past hour. Iranian state media suggested vessels could test the U.S. blockade, prompting Trump's warning that they would be sent to the bottom of the sea.
• *Military Situation:* Iranian forces reportedly struck U.S. troops in Bahrain overnight. Two U.S. aircraft carrier strike groups remain in the Arabian Sea, with American refueling aircraft in Israel. The conflict began February 28 with Operation Epic Fury.
• *Iran's Capabilities:* The Wall Street Journal reports Iran retains approximately 1,500 ballistic missiles and can manufacture around 50 monthly, despite earlier U.S. strikes targeting Iranian military capabilities and senior officials.
• *Diplomatic Efforts:* Indirect negotiations continue without a breakthrough. Qatar is relaying messages between Washington and Tehran, while Gulf allies seek a settlement over fears renewed fighting would trigger Iranian retaliation against regional energy infrastructure.
• *Domestic Unrest:* Protests have renewed inside Iran as authorities announced rolling power cuts. Trump said he had seen protest videos and encouraged demonstrators to continue.
